content.title: Prime Video's Scarpetta: A New Crime Thriller with Endless Potential
content.text: Published Mar 14, 2026, 12:30 PM EDT Liz Hersey is an Editor and Critic for ScreenRant's TV team, editing, reviewing, writing, and creating content about the iconic shows you love to watch. She began her editing career at ScreenRant in 2019, shortly after joining the site as a Writer that same year. With a passion for all things books, Liz frequently attends Toronto literary events and conferences, and loves interacting with her book lover community. In addition to being an avid reader of the romance and thriller genres, Liz is a writer of several short stories, and is currently at work on a young adult witch novel. When she's not working, reading, or writing, Liz can be found seeing movies at her local cinema, attending live jazz events, or curling up on the couch to binge her favorite TV shows. You can reach her at liz.h@screenrant.com. Sign in to your Screen Rant account Perhaps even more exciting than the sheer volume of Scarpetta's A-list stars is the fact that it could be Prime Video's next long-running crime thriller series. Scarpetta debuted with a commendable Rotten Tomatoes score — it is currently Certified Fresh at 76% — on March 11, with Prime Video releasing all eight episodes of the first season at once. Based on Patricia Cornwell's book series of the same name, Scarpetta's cast is led by Nicole Kidman as the titular forensic pathologist, and she's joined by an ensemble of decorated actors that includes Jamie Lee Curtis, Bobby Cannavale, and Ariana DeBose. In season 1, Kidman's Dr. Kay Scarpetta returns to her position as Virginia Chief Medical Examiner, only to be haunted by the past when a new serial killer's MO resembles one of Scarpetta's cases from 28 years ago. Scarpetta Is Based On A Book Series With 29 Novels Many crime thriller shows run out of story quickly, but with Patricia Cornwell's Scarpetta series consisting of 29 books thus far, that won't be a problem for the Prime Video adaptation. Scarpetta season 1 features a dual timeline, flipping back and forth between present-day 2026 and 1998, when Dr. Scarpetta (Rosy McEwen) is brand new to the job. To tell the story this way, the season adapts book #1 of Cornwell's series, Postmortem (1990), and book #25, Autospy (2021). Prime Video is also the perfect platform for Scarpetta, given the streamer's history of successful crime thriller series adaptations. Based on the novel series by Michael Connelly, Bosch is one of the most successful and enduring Prime Video series of all time, running for seven seasons and spawning two spinoffs, Bosch: Legacy and Ballard, the latter of which is still airing. Similarly, Reacher, based on Lee Child's Jack Reacher books, is going into its fourth season and shows no sign of slowing down. Reacher is also getting a spinoff called Neagley, which is expected to release sometime later this year. Finally, James Patterson's iconic Alex Cross novels have had many adaptations, with the currently running Prime Video series, Cross​​​​​, considered one of the best. Cross's first season debuted to a 76% Rotten Tomatoes score — same as Scarpetta season 1 — and leapt up to 94% for season 2. All of this bodes incredibly well for Scarpetta. Scarpetta’s Short 8-Episode Season Means It Can Keep Its A-List Cast This is a bit of a concern when it comes to Scarpetta, as it boasts three Oscar winners in Nicole Kidman, Ariana DeBose, and Jamie Lee Curtis. The prolific Bobby Cannavale is also a two-time Emmy winner who typically makes three or more movies a year in addition to his TV projects. Even if the source material is there for multiple seasons of Scarpetta, the actors may not be. However, season 1 is only eight episodes long, and if future seasons remain that way, it makes for a manageable commitment from Scarpetta's starry cast. The dual timeline also helps with this because, rather than Kidman having to anchor eight hour-long episodes per season, she's only in it for half the time, with Rose McEwen taking over for the rest. Furthermore, both Kidman and Curtis serve as Scarpetta producers through their production companies, Blossom Films and Comet Pictures, respectively. (Comet Productions is co-owned by Blumhouse Television.) It's in their interests for Scarpetta to be a long-running and successful, and with the show calling Prime Video its home, all signs point to it being just that. Release Date March 11, 2026 Network Prime Video Showrunner Elizabeth Sarnoff Cast Directors David Gordon Green, Charlotte Brändström Creator(s) Elizabeth Sarnoff
